purpose: Separate the 14 September 1735 Louisiana card-money ceiling from retrospective distribution claims, the 27 April 1744 recall declaration, Surrey's separate 30 April 1744 issue-order report, and the unresolved 1746 allowance/exchange lead. This is not a financial-flow ledger.

records.claim: Zay's 1892 reproduction of the ordinance authorizes up to 200,000 livres nominal card money and requires records for each fabrication. It is an authorization, not evidence of completed fabrication or issue.

The declaration says 1735 card money had been distributed for royal expenses and describes recall/redemption procedures. Because it is a later royal declaration in the same 1892 compilation, it supports a retrospective official distribution claim but not exact issuance, independent corroboration, completed recall, or payment.

records.reported_terms: five-to-two basis; intended circulation two months after publication
records.claim: Surrey reports a separate 30 April 1744 order and says implementation was deferred. This is not the 27 April recall declaration; no original text or actual issue is verified.

records.archival_locator: Surrey (1916), printed p.138, footnote 4: AN C13, vol.31 fol.139
records.claim: Surrey reports that a 200,000-livre allowance was used in return for Spanish silver expended on fortifications at English Turn and Mobile. The underlying folio was not examined; it is unresolved which issue/allowance this describes and whether it connects to the 1735 authorization or 30 April 1744 order. No transaction or payment is recorded.

archival_retrieval_targets.locator: AN C, Sér. A, vol.22 fol.146; vol.23 (14 Sep 1735); AN C, Sér. C13 vol.34 fols.376–378
archival_retrieval_targets.purpose: Resolve the 1735 ordinance's production/implementation and identify fabrication procès-verbaux; exact individual record and wording not yet checked.

archival_retrieval_targets.locator: AN C, Sér. B, vol.78 fols.42–51
archival_retrieval_targets.purpose: Examine the reported 30 April 1744 five-to-two card-money order and clarify why Surrey says implementation was deferred.
Examine the 1746 200,000-livre allowance/exchange lead and identify its relationship, if any, to the 1735 or 1744 instruments.

unresolved_relationships: Does the 1744 declaration's retrospective statement that 1735 cards were distributed refer to the full 200,000-livre ceiling or only some amount? It does not quantify actual issue.
Surrey says the 1735 project was realized some years later; exact implementation date and amount require the cited archives.
27 April 1744 recall declaration and 30 April 1744 issue order are separate by date and description. Their relationship, and whether the later issue order was executed, remain unresolved.
The 1746 200,000-livre allowance/exchange reference is not linked conclusively to a specific earlier instrument.
The colonial and royal statements about inhabitants' wishes are mediated administrative claims; no consultation record from Indigenous nations or enslaved people is established.
